summary:
Implemented the catalog/taxonomy/faceted-filtering epic end to end: a new shared `catalog` bounded context (occasion, card_style, product_category, recipient_segment, material, card_format, color_family, personalization_capability as one discriminated catalog_terms table, with real parent/child hierarchy for product_category), the previously-empty `card-catalog` and `product-catalog` module skeletons filled in with domain/application/infrastructure/presentation layers, four migrations, idempotent seed data matching the mau-thiep/qua-ky-niem prototypes, three public GET endpoints (/api/v1/catalogs, /api/v1/card-templates, /api/v1/products) with pagination, deterministic sort, search, multi-select filters and facet counts (AND across facets, OR within a facet, descendant-inclusive category counts, no M2M duplicate counting), full Swagger/OpenAPI documentation and a verified generated-document contract test. On the frontend: array-aware query serialization and typed catalogs/card-templates/products API wrappers generated from the backend's real OpenAPI schema, TanStack Query hooks with AbortSignal-based request cancellation, a URL-search-params-as-source-of-truth filter/search/sort/page hook, and both `/mau-thiep` and `/qua-ky-niem` migrated off local mock arrays onto the real API with loading/background-refresh/error-retry/empty/zero-count-disabled states, while preserving the existing MEMORIES-0003 layout and presentation components (adapted via view-model mapper functions instead of rewriting them).

Review-cycle-4 fix pass: fixed a boolean-query-param bug (`rush=false` silently read as `true` under global `enableImplicitConversion`; fixed with `@Type(() => String)` before the custom `@Transform`); restored the qua-ky-niem hero artwork on mobile/tablet; added 15 GiftCatalog integration tests; replaced the UI-fidelity capture script with a CDP-driven one that fails loudly on a browser error page and captures the full scrollable page.

Review-cycle-7 fix pass: refreshed stale handoff/migration-count evidence (3/9 -> 4/10) with a full isolated empty-database migration cycle rerun (apply x4/seed/e2e/revert x4/reapply/reseed/e2e, passing identically both times); recaptured 4 UI-fidelity entries that had been taken against a database the capture script's port-mismatched default never actually reached.

Validation-fix attempt 2: fixed a frontend-wide typecheck/build break in packages/config/src/env.ts — replaced an unsound `as NodeJS.ProcessEnv` cast with a narrow `PublicEnvSource` type matching the 6 keys `getAppEnv` actually reads.

Review-cycle-8 fix pass (backend-only): resolved 4 verified findings (full mechanism in `decisions` below): regenerated changed_files from `git diff`/`git ls-files`; added `CatalogTerm.reconcile()` so a seed rerun repairs manually-altered rows, not just skips them; fixed blank/malformed filter validation (AC12, `toIdArray` no longer drops empty CSV segments, numeric filters use `@Type(() => String)` + `toTrimmedNumber`); wrapped seed use-case saves in `UnitOfWork.withTransaction(...)` for atomicity. Full backend validation reran clean: lint/typecheck/test 282/61 (+5)/test:architecture/test:e2e 104/13 (+27 tests, +3 suites)/build/export:openapi, all 5 deterministic skill scripts.

Review-cycle-9 fix pass (full-plan scope): reverted a global CORP relaxation in `configureApp` that had no benefit (CORP doesn't restrict cors-mode `fetch()`, verified against MDN) and weakened a real protection — new security-headers.e2e-spec.ts (4 tests); fixed a dead search button/Enter-key submit in card-catalog.tsx, wrapped in `<form onSubmit>` like gift-catalog.tsx (2 new tests).

Review-cycle-10 fix pass (full-plan scope): fixed a stale "three migrations" summary sentence and re-audited every count in this document (446/1613 -> 447/1620); disabled zero-count derived-filter choices (gift-catalog rush checkbox, card-catalog access-tier radios) that stayed clickable while selected-but-zero stays clearable (4 new tests); added e2e coverage for 4 previously-untested product filter families plus 2 cross-facet AND cases, each picking ids dynamically from the live facets response. Full e2e suite now 114/14 (+6); public-web suite now 60/9 (+4).

Review-cycle-11 fix pass (backend-only, full-plan scope): `enforce_catalog_terms_hierarchy()` validated only the row being written against its own `parent_id`, never a row that OTHER rows reference via THEIR `parent_id` — an UPDATE changing a referenced PRODUCT_CATEGORY parent's catalog_type silently succeeded, leaving its child pointed at a now-wrongly-typed parent. Trigger now also rejects any catalog_type change on a row still referenced by another row's parent_id; new catalog-hierarchy-guard.e2e-spec.ts case proves the rejection; migration reverted+reapplied against live Postgres. Full backend validation reran clean (test:e2e 115/14 (+1), rest unchanged). Frontend unaffected.

Review-cycle-12 fix pass (full-plan scope): resolved 4 verified major findings. #1 rewrote price/preparation/rush facets as one bounded `COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN...)` query per facet in Postgres, replacing a Node-side load-every-matching-variant-then-Array.filter approach (new 24-variant e2e fixture). #2 added `status = 'ACTIVE'` to every catalog-term read path missing it (product/card-template link filters, category descendant closure, findDescendantIds), so a deactivated term stops being filterable/renderable/traversable (3 new real-Postgres regressions). #3 `mapProduct` mapped a null variant to a fabricated `price: 0`; `GiftProduct.price`/`Price` widened to `number | null`, rendering 'Đang cập nhật giá' instead (purchase controls already disabled via `inStock`); new integration test. #4 reran the full empty-database migration cycle against a freshly recreated Postgres database with all current-cycle code present. Full backend validation reran clean (test:e2e 119/15 (+4), rest unchanged, all 6 deterministic skill scripts); frontend reran clean (test 61/9 (+1)).

Validation-fix attempt 3: `npm run test:e2e` (the exact required command, invoked with no extra flags by both CI and this validation gate) was flaky under Jest's default parallel workers — every e2e spec file targets one shared live Postgres database, so concurrent spec files racing inserts/deletes against each other could shift a count-based assertion mid-run. Reproduced the reported failure locally (`products.e2e-spec.ts` "keeps derived price, preparation and rating facet counts consistent with their filters", expected 15 received 17 — a sibling spec's concurrently-created rows leaking into the assertion window), confirming this was the same DB-contention pattern review-cycle-12 had already documented as pre-existing but never fixed at the command level. Root-caused and fixed by setting `maxWorkers: 1` in `test/jest-e2e.json`, so `npm run test:e2e` itself is deterministic in every environment without relying on an operator remembering `--runInBand`. Reran twice locally after the fix: 119/119 passing both times.

Validation-fix attempt 3 adds test/jest-e2e.json (maxWorkers: 1). Review-cycle-13 fix modifies libs/modules/product-catalog/src/infrastructure/persistence/typeorm-product.repository.ts (computeRatingFacet) and apps/api/test/products.e2e-spec.ts (both already listed) — no new files.

decisions.decision: One shared `catalog.catalog_terms` table discriminated by `catalog_type`, instead of eight near-identical tables, for occasion/card_style/product_category/recipient_segment/material/card_format/color_family/personalization_capability.
decisions.reason: All eight share identical id/code/name/status/sort_order/timestamps shape; only product_category needs parent_id. One table with a discriminator avoids duplicating identical schema/domain/repository code eight times.

decisions.decision: New bounded context `libs/modules/catalog` (registered in tsconfig.json/nest-cli.json/business-modules.ts across api/worker/scheduler/cli) owns every centrally-managed catalog; `card-catalog` and `product-catalog` depend on it only through `CATALOG_TERMS_READER` from its public-api.ts, never its repository or ORM entity.
decisions.reason: Matches the Epic's technical-notes recommendation and keeps occasion genuinely shared (AC #3) without either module owning the other's taxonomy.

decisions.decision: Cross-module references from card_template_catalog_terms/product_catalog_terms to catalog_terms are plain UUID columns with no DB foreign key.
decisions.reason: Confirmed as the existing module-boundary convention (identity_access -> user_profiles is the precedent); referential integrity for cross-module ids is enforced at the application boundary (CatalogTermsReader) at seed/write time instead.

decisions.decision: product_category seeded with 2 parent + 7 leaf terms forming a real two-level tree (handmade-gifts, photo-personalized-gifts as parents), derived from the qua-ky-niem prototype's `cat` field; the prototype's 'Quà handmade'/'Combo thiệp và quà' filter tags are intentionally not modeled as categories, materials or a collection.
decisions.reason: Epic AC #4 requires a real, testable parent/child descendant-filter, not just schema capability. The two dropped prototype tags are collection-like labels the Epic allows deferring.

decisions.decision: swatch_hex is a nullable column on the shared catalog_terms table (only populated for COLOR_FAMILY rows) rather than a separate per-type side table.
decisions.reason: Avoids an EAV model for one optional presentation field while keeping every other catalog type's rows unaffected; documented in catalog-term.ts.

decisions.decision: Facet counts: for catalog-term-backed facets (card: occasion/style/format/colorFamily/accessTier; product: category/occasion/recipient/personalization/material/rush) each facet's own option counts are computed excluding only that facet's own active filter, with every other active filter (including price/prep/rush/rating for products) still applied — implemented as a per-facet `buildMatchConditions`/`buildConditions` call parameterized by an `exclude` key.
decisions.reason: Matches the Epic's count definition; verified with an e2e test that a nonexistent-occasion filter zeroes every other facet while occasion keeps its own count.

decisions.decision: product_category facet counts are descendant-inclusive via a recursive `WITH RECURSIVE` closure CTE over parent_id, not just direct-assignment counts.
decisions.reason: Selecting a parent category must let a user browse everything under it (Epic AC #4); the same closure powers the category FILTER via `CatalogTermsReader.resolveDescendantIds`, called once from the use case before the repository sees the filter.

decisions.decision: Price/preparation/rating remain derived query attributes rather than catalog tables, but the product response exposes UI-aligned derived facet groups with counts for the documented price, cumulative preparation and minimum-rating options.
decisions.reason: The Epic forbids persistent bucket catalogs, not response-time derived counts. TypeormProductRepository computes all three from effective product/variant data, and products.e2e-spec.ts now compares every derived option count with the corresponding real filtered query.

decisions.decision: Each seeded product has one representative variant (schema supports many); list filtering and the displayed/sorted effective offer use the same cheapest available variant satisfying all requested price/preparation/rush conditions through a filtered LATERAL selection.
decisions.reason: Epic caps commerce-lifecycle modeling; one variant per product is the minimal model satisfying 'sellable variant/offer', while the schema isn't restricted to 1:1 for future extension.

decisions.decision: Bug fix: card-catalog's `buildMatchConditions` now takes an explicit `startIndex` param (0 for `computeAccessTierFacet`, 1 for `computeCatalogFacet`) instead of a hardcoded `paramIndex = 1`.
decisions.reason: Found via e2e testing: a search/filter-only request crashed with a Postgres 'could not determine data type of parameter $1' error because the old code always started numbering at $2. product-catalog's repository already used this pattern correctly.

decisions.decision: Bug fix: `ListProductsUseCase` now falls back to the original (unexpanded) `categoryIds` when `resolveDescendantIds` returns an empty set for a nonexistent-but-syntactically-valid id, instead of passing an empty array through.
decisions.reason: The repository treats empty categoryIds as 'no filter'; without the fallback, a nonexistent category id matched everything instead of nothing, violating AC #12.

decisions.decision: Backend page/pageSize query fields got an explicit `type: Number` added to their `@ApiPropertyOptional` decorator.
decisions.reason: `@nestjs/swagger` can't infer a type from a bare `page = 1` initializer without an explicit hint, so page/pageSize were silently missing from the exported OpenAPI spec (a pre-existing gap elsewhere too, left untouched as out of scope).

decisions.decision: Formatting-only fix: collapsed multi-line `@ApiResponse({...})` decorators (auth.controller.ts and the three new controllers) to single-line.
decisions.reason: check_openapi_contract.py's brace-boundary heuristic misidentified a multi-line decorator's closing `})` as the previous method's, truncating the captured block. Zero behavior change; required to make the deterministic skill script pass.

decisions.decision: Frontend: array-valued query params are serialized as one comma-joined value (`ids=a,b,c`), never repeated keys, in `ApiClient.buildUrl`.
decisions.reason: Matches every list DTO's `class-transformer` `@Transform` (`split(',')`) convention on the backend exactly — verified with a query-serialization test asserting the exact encoded URL.

decisions.decision: `ApiClientProvider`/`useApiClient()` context added in `apps/public-web/lib/api/` (app-local), not in `packages/api-client`.
decisions.reason: `packages/api-client` has no React dependency at all (a deliberate framework-agnostic fetch wrapper) — adding a React context provider there would introduce a new dependency against the package's existing design intent. The app already owns the single `ApiClient` instance in `app/providers.tsx`; the context just exposes that same instance.

decisions.decision: URL is the single source of truth for filter/search/sort/page state (`useUrlFilterState`, backed by `next/navigation`'s `useSearchParams`/`useRouter`/`usePathname`), replacing the previous local-`useState`-only filter model; catalog-term selections are stored as stable `code`s in the URL, resolved to ids client-side once catalog-term metadata loads (an unresolvable code from a stale URL is silently dropped, never crashes).
decisions.reason: Filter/search/sort/page must be shareable/restorable via reload/back/forward; codes are the Epic's own stable/shareable unit vs. opaque ids.

decisions.decision: Manual 'load more' cumulative-fetch pagination (MEMORIES-0003 mock UI) was replaced with real Prev/Next page-number pagination reflected in the URL, same button-based visual style.
decisions.reason: The backend is genuinely page-based, and the Epic requires the URL to reflect page and reset to page 1 on filter change — 'load more' has no single well-defined page to put in the URL.

decisions.decision: `GiftProduct.image`/`.rating` are now `string | null` / `number | null` end-to-end (no fallback string substituted); `ProductCard`/`QuickViewDialog`/the homepage `GiftsTeaser` render an explicit 'Chưa có ảnh'/'Chưa có đánh giá' state instead.
decisions.reason: API contract permits both fields null, so the UI keeps explicit missing-image/missing-rating states instead of coercing nulls. Seed data supplies the prototype's real assets/ratings.

decisions.decision: `GiftProduct.colors`/`.sizes` are always `null`, `.requiresOptions` is always `false`; per-product color/size purchase options are not modeled.
decisions.reason: Per-product color/size variant axes are not part of the Epic's domain model (out of scope, same category as the deferred collection/rule engine) — the mock data's colors/sizes were presentation-only fixtures with no corresponding backend field.

decisions.decision: `CardTemplate.motif` is a constant `'minimal'`; `.background`/`.foreground` are derived from the template's real color-family `swatchHex` (with a luminance-based readable-foreground fallback) instead of the prototype's fabricated per-item motif/colors.
decisions.reason: No per-item generated-art field exists in the real domain model; reusing the real color-family term keeps card art tied to real data, and `TemplateThumbnail`'s existing `'minimal'`-fallback path needed zero changes.

decisions.decision: `ProductCard` badges and `prepLabel` text are derived in `mapProduct()` from real fields (isNew, rating thresholds, personalization codes, variant prep window) instead of the prototype's hand-curated per-item badge arrays.
decisions.reason: The backend has no curated-badges field; deriving from real thresholds keeps badges truthful and reuses the existing `BADGE_VARIANT` map.

decisions.decision: Review-cycle-4 bug fix: `ListProductsQueryDto.rush` now has `@Type(() => String)` added before its existing `@Transform`/`@IsBoolean`, instead of relying on the bare `boolean` design-type.
decisions.reason: Root-caused via live-Postgres e2e: with implicit conversion on, class-transformer re-derives via Boolean(rawValue) after the custom @Transform, so rush=false silently became true. Pinning to String makes @Transform final.

decisions.decision: Review-cycle-4: rewrote the `rush=true`/`rush=false` facet-counts-sum-to-total e2e assertion to explicitly account for genuine multi-variant overlap instead of asserting a strict partition.
decisions.reason: The old `trueCount + falseCount === total` assertion only held when no product could match both filter values — no longer true once a product can have variants on each side of a boundary. The rewrite computes the real overlap and asserts the counts diverge from the total by exactly that amount.

decisions.decision: Review-cycle-4: `qua-ky-niem/page.tsx`'s hero image composition changed from `hidden ... lg:block` to always-rendered with `order-last` and viewport-scaled `min-h` (220px mobile / 300px tablet / 380px desktop), instead of building a second, simplified mobile-only asset.
decisions.reason: The composition already uses fill/percentage-width Images inside a relative container, so it scales at any height without new assets; order-last keeps DOM/visual order correct on every breakpoint.

decisions.decision: Review-cycle-4: new GiftCatalog tests reuse the exact loading/retry/stale-response/pagination-reset patterns already established in `card-catalog.spec.tsx` rather than inventing a new testing style.
decisions.reason: Keeps the two catalog test suites structurally symmetric with equivalent coverage; also adds product-specific coverage CardCatalog doesn't need (multi-facet AND/OR serialization, zero-count disabled-state, nullable image/rating rendering).

decisions.decision: Review-cycle-4: UI-fidelity evidence is produced by `.ai/validation/ui-fidelity/capture-fidelity.mjs`, a CDP script over Node's built-in fetch/WebSocket, replacing the previous plain `chrome --screenshot` script.
decisions.reason: The prior script silently saved a browser error page as passed evidence and only captured the viewport rect. The new script fails loudly on an error page and captures the full scrollable page via Fetch.enable.

decisions.decision: Validation-fix attempt 2: `packages/config/src/env.ts`'s `processEnvSnapshot`/`getAppEnv`'s `source` param are typed as a local `PublicEnvSource` (the 6 public env keys) instead of `NodeJS.ProcessEnv`; the unsound trailing `as NodeJS.ProcessEnv` cast was removed.
decisions.reason: typecheck/build failed with TS2352 because the snapshot literal only ever had 6 keys, never the rest of `ProcessEnv`'s shape. `getAppEnv` only reads those 6 named properties, so narrowing the type is correct and needs no cast.

decisions.decision: Review-cycle-8 fix #2: added `CatalogTerm.reconcile(changes, now)` so a seed rerun repairs manually-altered rows instead of skipping existing ones.
decisions.reason: SeedCatalogTermsUseCase's existing-row branch previously no-opped; reconcile() re-validates create()'s invariants and updates drifted fields. 5 unit tests + catalog-seed-convergence.e2e-spec.ts.

decisions.decision: Review-cycle-8 fix #3: `toIdArray` no longer drops empty CSV segments after trimming; priceMin/priceMax/prepWithinDays/ratingMin switched from bare `@Type(() => Number)` to `@Type(() => String)` + a `@Transform` mapping blank to NaN.
decisions.reason: A blank/comma-only/inner-empty CSV filter value was silently read as 'no filter' instead of a validation error (AC12); `Number('')===0` also silently passed blank numeric params as 0. `@IsNumber()`/`@IsInt()` reject NaN by default.

decisions.decision: Review-cycle-8 fix #4: `SeedProductsUseCase`/`SeedCardTemplatesUseCase` now wrap their save call in `UnitOfWork.withTransaction(...)`.
decisions.reason: The multi-statement save+delete+reinsert sequence wasn't atomic; 2 new e2e specs force a mid-save unique-constraint violation and prove the aggregate is never partially committed.

decisions.decision: Review-cycle-8 post-fix hardening: catalog-seed-convergence.e2e-spec.ts's first test no longer toggles a term's own row directly, avoiding cross-test interference.
decisions.reason: Keeps the convergence regression isolated to its own fixture instead of mutating shared seeded rows other tests depend on.

decisions.decision: Review-cycle-9 fix: `configureApp` reverted from a relaxed `crossOriginResourcePolicy: 'cross-origin'` helmet config back to plain `helmet()`.
decisions.reason: CORP doesn't restrict cors-mode fetch() (verified via MDN), so the relaxation had no benefit and weakened a real protection; new security-headers.e2e-spec.ts proves public endpoints stay reachable cross-origin and a protected route keeps the header.

decisions.decision: Review-cycle-9 fix: card-catalog.tsx's search bar wrapped in a `<form onSubmit>`/`type="submit"`, mirroring gift-catalog.tsx, replacing a bare `<div>` with a dead `type="button"`.
decisions.reason: The search input didn't submit on Enter, an accessibility/UX gap gift-catalog.tsx didn't have; 2 new tests.

decisions.decision: Review-cycle-10 fix: gift-catalog.tsx's rush checkbox and card-catalog.tsx's access-tier radios now disable an unselected zero-count option while keeping a selected zero-count option clearable.
decisions.reason: Matches the price/prep/rating/TermFilterGroup pattern already used elsewhere; previously both stayed clickable at count 0, letting a user trigger an avoidable empty request.

decisions.decision: Review-cycle-10 fix: the new cross-facet AND e2e cases in products.e2e-spec.ts/card-templates.e2e-spec.ts pick their filter option ids dynamically from the live, already-narrowed facets response rather than hardcoding seed codes/ids.
decisions.reason: Guarantees each combined filter genuinely co-occurs on at least one real seeded row instead of gambling on independently-chosen ids that might intersect to an empty (and therefore untestable) result, and keeps the tests resilient to future seed-data edits.

decisions.decision: Review-cycle-11 fix: `enforce_catalog_terms_hierarchy()` now rejects an UPDATE changing catalog_type on a row still referenced by another row's parent_id.
decisions.reason: The trigger only validated a written row against its own parent_id, never rows referencing it — an UPDATE on a referenced PRODUCT_CATEGORY parent's catalog_type silently succeeded, leaving children pointed at a wrongly-typed parent. New catalog-hierarchy-guard.e2e-spec.ts case (6/6) proves the rejection and that both rows stay unchanged; migration reverted+reapplied against live Postgres to pick up the fix.

decisions.decision: Review-cycle-12 fix #1: computePriceFacet/computePreparationFacet/computeRushFacet rewritten as a single bounded `COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN <bucket> THEN p.id END)` query per facet (computeBucketFacet), replacing fetchMatchingVariantsByProduct which SELECTed every matching variant and bucketed them in Node.
decisions.reason: task.md forbids loading the full matching dataset into memory for facet counting; a new 24-variant e2e fixture asserts each of the 3 bucketed queries returns exactly one aggregated row, not one row per variant.

decisions.decision: Review-cycle-12 fix #2: added `status = 'ACTIVE'` to every catalog-term read path missing it — TypeOrmCatalogTermRepository.findDescendantIds' recursive CTE (root + each hop), TypeOrmProductRepository's loadCatalogTermRefs/link-filter EXISTS/category closure CTE, and TypeOrmCardTemplateRepository's equivalents.
decisions.reason: Deactivating a term only hid it from GET /catalogs while still filterable, still shown on linked items, and still traversed by an active parent's descendant closure. Now a directly-supplied inactive UUID is an empty match; new catalog-inactive-terms.e2e-spec.ts covers product links, product category closure, and card-template links.

decisions.decision: Review-cycle-12 fix #3: `GiftProduct.price`/`Price`'s `amount` prop widened to `number | null`; `mapProduct` now maps a null `variant` to `price: null` instead of `?? 0`; `Price` renders an explicit 'Đang cập nhật giá' label instead of a currency amount when null.
decisions.reason: The backend intentionally allows an active product to have no available variant; ProductCard/QuickViewDialog were both rendering a fabricated 0 ₫ instead of an unavailable state. Purchase controls were already disabled via the existing `inStock` (= variant !== null) check, so no button-logic change was needed. New gift-catalog.spec.tsx integration test covers card + quick-view for a variant:null response.

decisions.decision: Review-cycle-12 fix #4: reran the full empty-database migration cycle (apply x4/seed/e2e/revert x4/reapply/reseed/e2e) against a freshly recreated `memories_clean_ci_test` Postgres database, with all review-cycle-12 code changes present.
decisions.reason: The prior empty-database evidence (review-cycle-7) predated every fix since; it no longer proved the current migration works from empty state. All steps passed; at that point the full suite was deterministic only under --runInBand (parallel workers contended for the same DB), a gap closed by the validation-fix-attempt-3 change below.

decisions.decision: Validation-fix attempt 3: added `"maxWorkers": 1` to `test/jest-e2e.json`, so `npm run test:e2e` (used verbatim by both CI and this validation gate, with no `--runInBand` flag) runs every e2e spec file serially instead of Jest's CPU-core-count-based default parallelism.
decisions.reason: Root cause, not a workaround: every e2e spec file in apps/api/test/ opens connections against the same live `memories-test-postgres` database and several specs assert exact row/facet counts; under default parallel workers, concurrent spec files racing inserts/deletes against shared tables can shift a count mid-assertion. Reproduced the exact reported failure locally (products.e2e-spec.ts's facet-count-vs-total assertion, expected 15 got 17) under default parallel workers, then confirmed 119/119 clean twice in a row after pinning maxWorkers to 1. This was already documented as a known pattern after review-cycle-12 but the fix had never been applied to the actual command CI/validation invoke, so the flake kept recurring across validation attempts.

decisions.decision: Review-cycle-13 fix (major, full-plan scope): computeRatingFacet rewritten as a bounded `COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.rating_average >= $N THEN p.id END)` aggregate per bucket, matching computeBucketFacet's price/preparation/rush pattern, via the same effectiveVariantLateralSql guard.
decisions.reason: Codex found computeRatingFacet fetched one rating_average row per matching product and bucketed in Node (unbounded memory, no scalability coverage). Fixed to match the other bucket facets; extended the large-set e2e regression to assert 4 bounded aggregate queries (was 3), each one row. Full backend validation set + all skill scripts rerun clean; no API/DTO surface change.

assumptions: Vietnamese-to-English catalog `code` slugs (e.g. 'birthday', 'velvet-wire-flowers', 'photo-based') are an editorial choice made for this implementation; no prior stable slug list existed to reconcile against.

The 'Quà khắc tên' personalization concept from the prototype maps to the seeded `name-engraving` personalization-capability term; a few prototype personalization labels with no corresponding Epic-taxonomy term (e.g. 'Gắn mã QR kỷ niệm') were intentionally omitted from seed data rather than invented as new catalog terms.

Card-template 'features' badges shown on `TemplateCard` are derived from the template's real pagesCount + card_format terms (e.g. '2 trang', 'Thiệp động') rather than the prototype's separate hand-authored features list, since the backend has no dedicated features field.

UI fidelity was refreshed with the task-owned headless-Chrome capture script against the current worktree and real local API at 375x812, 768x1024 and 1440x900, covering populated/selected-filter/empty states.
Review-cycle-4: both repos' dev servers and the required Postgres/Redis/MinIO containers were running in this environment; all fix verification ran against real local servers, never mocked.

Document two variant-selection SQL conventions from typeorm-product.repository.ts: (1) the LATERAL-join 'cheapest matching variant' pattern (`effectiveVariantLateralSql`) for list/sort/rating; (2) the 'every matching variant, not just cheapest' pattern (`fetchMatchingVariantsByProduct`) required for price/preparation/rush facets, since a single representative variant under-counts a product with variants on each side of a bucket boundary (review-cycle-4 fix: switched those 3 facets from (1) to (2)). Also document the recursive closure-CTE pattern for parent/child facet aggregation, and the DB-level BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger pattern (AddCatalogTermsHierarchyGuard) for cycle-detection invariants a plain self-FK can't express.

Document a real bug/fix as a required convention: with the global ValidationPipe's `enableImplicitConversion: true`, a DTO boolean/numeric query-param field decorated only with a custom `@Transform` gets silently overridden by class-transformer's implicit primitive-conversion step (e.g. `?flag=false` becomes `true`; a blank numeric string becomes `0`, not `NaN`, silently passing `@Min(0)`) — `@Type(() => Number)`'s conversion runs before any co-located `@Transform` regardless of decorator order. Fix: add `@Type(() => String)` before the custom `@Transform` to pin the implicit-conversion type away from the real target type, so the `@Transform` output is final (see `rush` in list-products.dto.ts; `toTrimmedNumber` for priceMin/priceMax/prepWithinDays/ratingMin). Companion CSV-array rule: `toIdArray`-style helpers must NOT `.filter(Boolean)` after splitting/trimming — a blank/inner-empty segment must survive as an empty string so `@IsUUID`/`@IsIn { each: true }` rejects it instead of being silently dropped.

Document the seed-convergence convention: an idempotent find-by-code-or-create seed use case must reconcile (update) an already-existing row's mutable fields onto the canonical seed definition, not just skip it, or a rerun only guarantees row *presence*, not row *content* — a manually-altered or stale-from-an-earlier-code-change row is never repaired. See `CatalogTerm.reconcile()` (libs/modules/catalog/src/domain/catalog-term/catalog-term.ts) + `SeedCatalogTermsUseCase.findOrCreate`'s existing-row branch for the reference implementation: re-validate the same invariants `create()` checks (duplicated, not extracted into a shared validator, matching the existing `UserProfile.update`/`Account.activate` convention), never reconcile the row's stable lookup identity fields (here: `code`/`catalogType`).

Document the transaction-boundary convention for multi-statement aggregate-replace methods (e.g. 'save aggregate, then delete+reinsert child rows', seen in `TypeOrmProductRepository.saveWithVariantsAndCatalogLinks`/`TypeOrmCardTemplateRepository.saveWithCatalogLinks`): the repository never opens the transaction itself — it only checks `TypeOrmQueryRunnerContext.get()` via `repositoryFor()`-style accessors. The CALLING use case wraps the whole call in `UnitOfWork.withTransaction(...)` (see `SeedProductsUseCase.seedOne`, matching `CreateAccountUseCase`). Any such delete+reinsert method called without that wrapper is not atomic — verify with an e2e test forcing a mid-sequence unique-constraint violation (two rows sharing a unique key in one insert batch is a reliable, self-contained way to do this) and asserting the aggregate row was not committed.

The 'chưa có page nào thật sự gọi useQuery/useMutation' statement is now outdated — /mau-thiep and /qua-ky-niem are the first real consumers. Document the ApiClientProvider (apps/public-web/lib/api/api-client-context.tsx) pattern for exposing the single ApiClient instance to hooks, and the useUrlFilterState URL-as-source-of-truth pattern, as the reference for future data-driven pages.
